scenario.title: Working at Height
scenario.summary: Safety principles for working above ground level.
scenario.mission: Identify unsafe working at height practices. Check equipment and follow the hierarchy of controls.

hazards.title: Overreaching on ladder
hazards.feedback: Correct. Overreaching can cause the ladder to tip over. Move the ladder instead.
hazards.reviewText: Never overreach while on a ladder. Keep your belt buckle inside the stiles.

hazards.title: Tools left unsecured at height
hazards.feedback: Correct. Unsecured tools can fall and injure people below.
hazards.reviewText: Secure all tools and materials when working at height.

hazards.title: Ladder on uneven surface
hazards.feedback: Correct. Ladders must always be placed on firm, level ground.
hazards.reviewText: Ensure stable footing for all access equipment.

hazards.title: Climbing with items in hands
hazards.feedback: Correct. You must maintain three points of contact when climbing.
hazards.reviewText: Keep hands free when climbing. Use a tool belt or hoist.

questions.prompt: What is the first step in the Working at Height hierarchy of controls?
questions.explanation: The primary goal is to avoid working at height if the task can be done safely from the ground.

options.label: Avoid working at height completely if possible

questions.prompt: How many points of contact should be maintained on a ladder?
questions.explanation: Maintain at least three points of contact (two feet and one hand, or two hands and one foot).

questions.prompt: What should you check before using a ladder?
questions.explanation: A visual inspection for damage must be done before every use.

options.label: That it is the right color
That it is free from defects and damage

questions.prompt: What is the 'belt buckle rule' for ladder safety?
questions.explanation: Keeping your belt buckle between the stiles prevents overreaching and tipping.

options.label: Keep your belt buckle between the ladder stiles
Buckle the ladder to the wall

questions.prompt: Who is responsible for ensuring safety when working at height?
questions.explanation: Everyone has a responsibility, both employers (to provide safe equipment) and employees (to use it safely).

options.label: Both the employer and the employee
Only the health and safety manager
Only the person doing the work
